headline: OpenAI has updated its Dots always-on agents so people can create one from the ChatGPT phone app and link it to Codex work.
score_reason: Pool 5 kept: a small feature update to a product launched days ago, reported by a minor outlet quoting OpenAI.
importance_line: What changed is that Dots can now be set up on a phone and can pick up work from OpenAI's coding and task tools, which affects early ChatGPT users first, then developers, and the doubt is that the article relays OpenAI's own post with no independent testing.
summary: The Tech Outlook reports that OpenAI has updated Dots, the always-on agents it introduced a few days ago that run on their own cloud computer and work towards a user's goals around the clock, so that a user can now create a dot in the ChatGPT app on iOS and Android, naming it, changing its look and connecting plugins. A dot can also start work in Codex, OpenAI's coding agent, follow up on existing Codex threads, search past ChatGPT conversations and read and edit ChatGPT Work automations, and our 8 Oct edition carried WIRED's test of Dots, which found it clumsy at shopping.
notes: Follow-up of Dots coverage (The Register on 7 Oct 2026, pool only; WIRED test in our 8 Oct edition). The date of OpenAI's update post is not stated, so it is treated as new today.
